To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) highly organized stacked multlaminar layers can be obtained via LBL assembly of polyelectroyltes and lipid-like surfactans; 2) the multilayers can be used to host ferrocene redox units and to create spatially addressable bioelectrochemical interfaces.

highly-organized multilayers can be obtained by layer-by-layer assembly using lipid-like surfactats and that the resulting stratified multilayrs can be used as hosts for redox-active species and enzymes.

we have developed a novel strategy for the preparation of highly stratified supramolecular multilayers with spatially-addressed functionalities, which can be used for (bio)chemical and electrochemical nanoarchitectonic applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of supramolecular self-organizing systems for the preparation of stratified multilayres.
the design of novel supramolecular structures with high degree of organization for the development of advanced functional materials for "nanoarchitectonic" applications.
the development of a novel supramolecular strategy for the construction of highly stratified multilamellar films with potential application as functional materials for (bio)electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results represent a major advance in the development of novel supramolecular materials for (bio)electronics and nanoarchitectoncs.

the use of the lipid-like surfactan dodecylphosphate in the LbL assembly process leads to highly organized stratified multilamellar films with well-defined hydrophilic/hyrophobic domains oriented parallel with the substrate.
we have developed a facile method for the fabrication of highly-ordered stacked multilayers with well-defined internal structure and with a high degree of control over the molecular architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present work provides a simple method to create highly organized stacked multibilayers through simple methods, and the multilayers can be used as a platform for (bio)chemical and (bio)electronic applications.

the present work provides an efficient and versatile approach for the preparation of well-defined stratified supramolecular multilayered structures, which are of interest for the development of (bio)electrocatalytic devices.
highly-organized stacked multlaminar films with well-defined hydrophilic/hypdrophobic domains can be prepared through simple layer-by-layer self-assembly of polyelectrotyes and lipid-like surfactans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of lipid-like surfacants and polyelelectrolytes allows for the construction of highly-organized stacked multlayers, with potential for the development of (bio)electrical devices.

highly-organized stacked multilevel architectures can be readily prepared using simple and straightforward procedures, thus paving the way to the design of novel functional materials for emerging applications in (bio)electronic devices.

the use of a lipid-like surfacant as structure-directing agent in layer-by-layer assembly is a powerful strategy for creating highly stratified multilayes with a wide range of potential applications in nanoarchitectonices.
